mechanism.name: Fong-Yiu bounded cubic quantile distribution: marginal 0.9 quantile

generation_equations.label: Equivalent inverse-transform construction
generation_equations.expression: U_i iid ~ Uniform(0,1); Y_i=4(U_i-0.4)^3+0.2U_i. No added noise; only Y is observed.

generation_equations.label: Independent verification route
generation_equations.expression: Q*(u)=4u^3-4.8u^2+2.12u-0.256; F_Y(y) is the unique inverse root in [0,1] on the support, with 0/1 outside.

sampling.unit: one fully observed scalar response Y per row
sampling.dependence: iid across rows; no clustering, serial dependence or interference structure
sampling.n_semantics: n is the actual requested row count and overrides nominal paper_n; the latter is design metadata only.
sampling.cross_scenario_coupling: Author script uses n=50 as prefix of a single n=500 sample. Local generator yields prefixes for matching seed across n; iid refers to rows within a dataset, not independence of scenarios sharing a seed.

assumptions: Independent and identically distributed scalar observations from the declared P*: explicitly stated in publisher Section 7.1 journal p.1152 (PDF p.23), consistent with arXiv v1 p.25.
Y is fully observed; no selection, censoring or missingness is introduced. The simulator has no covariates; U is internal inverse-transform randomness, not an observed covariate.
Derived regularity: Q is continuous and Q'(u)=12(u-0.4)^2+0.2>=0.2 on [0,1], so the marginal quantile is unique and F has positive continuous density at the interior target.
The target is a functional of the observed marginal distribution. At Q(0.9)=0.68 the density is 0.3125. No causal intervention, confounding, cross-world or mediation assumptions apply.

properties.notes: dimension/effective_dimension count observed input covariates: both 0. There is one response Y and one internal Uniform variable U. Nonlinearity is 4(U-0.4)^3; powers of one scalar are not multivariable interactions. No high-dimensional or confounding claim. Bounded support [-0.256,1.064], f_Y(Q(.9))=.3125.

estimand.name: theta = Q_Y(0.9)
estimand.definition: Marginal population quantile inf{y: P(Y<=y)>=0.9} under Y=4(U-0.4)^3+0.2U, U~Uniform(0,1); no conditioning variables or interventions. The fixed query is tau=0.9 in both scenarios.

parameters.description: Original bounded cubic distribution at paper sample size n=50; fixed tau=.9 is the declared target adaptation.

truth.expression: Marginal population quantile inf{y: P(Y<=y)>=0.9} under Y=4(U-0.4)^3+0.2U, U~Uniform(0,1); no conditioning variables or interventions. The fixed query is tau=0.9 in both scenarios.
truth.derivation: Strictly increasing inverse transform: Q_Y(tau)=4(tau-.4)^3+.2*tau. Fraction arithmetic yields exact 17/25; independent Decimal expanded-polynomial CDF inversion plus uniform/center analytic cases. Float conversion error is reported separately from sampling/source uncertainty.

parameters.description: Original bounded cubic distribution at paper sample size n=500; fixed tau=.9 is the declared target adaptation.

adaptations: Preserve the paper analytic cubic distribution and n=50/n=500; restrict to scalar tau=.9. Author code instead implements a finite-grid interpolant with flat tails, so paper-law preservation does not imply exact author-code distribution reproduction.

Use direct cubic evaluation with local Python random.Random, instead of author NumPy global seed 2024 and np.interp over a JAX interior grid. Author n=50/500 data are nested prefixes; this local generator also has prefix coupling when called with the same seed at different n. No claim to author samples, posterior fitting or Figure 4 reproduction.

Declare original_n50 and original_n500 as two scenarios of one mechanism. The n argument controls generated row count; paper_n records the original design. CLI smoke checks use n=128 and verify additionally generates each original nominal sample size.
Linear-only and tau=0.4 cases are auxiliary verification cases, not additional source scenarios or new mechanism families.

2026-11-01 numerical endpoint correction only: for random draw u=0 evaluate -a*b^3 using exact decimal-parameter fractions before float conversion; all nonzero draws use the previous expression. No clipping, changed schema, parameter or population law.
